# BLO-39114 — reap the stale run's pod log when the admission path reaps its Job

[BLO-39114](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-39114) ·
`src/server/execute.ts`, `src/server/job-manifest.ts`, plus both test files

The concurrency-admission path deletes a **different** run's Job when that run
is terminal or missing in Paperclip, and called `cleanupJob` without a
`podLogPath`. `reapPodLogFile` returns immediately on its `if (!podLogPath)`
guard, so that run's `<runId>.pod.ndjson` stayed on the shared PVC forever.

This is the second producer of the leak [BLO-32734](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-32734)
measured (≥20,480 orphaned files). [#1724](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1724)
fixed the unlink for a run's *own* log. This one covers the runs that die
before ever reaching their own `cleanupJob` — pod OOM, node eviction,
`job_failed` — which BLO-32734's AC2 expected would need a sweeper. No sweeper
is needed: this path already knows which run it is reaping and is already
deleting that run's Job. It only lacked the path.

## Why the path is stamped, not reconstructed

The path could be rebuilt from the Job's labels, which carry all four inputs to
`buildPodLogPath`. That was rejected. `companyId`, `agentId` and `runId` each
reach the **path** through `sanitizeForK8sPath` and the **label** through
`sanitizeLabelValue`, from the same raw value, and those two are not equivalent:

| | `sanitizeForK8sPath` (path) | `sanitizeLabelValue` (label) |
|---|---|---|
| `.` and `_` | stripped | kept |
| length | unbounded | truncated at 63 |
| leading/trailing non-alnum | kept | trimmed |
| no usable chars | `""` | `null` |

Today all three are UUIDs, for which the two agree — so the divergence is
**latent, not active**. That is an argument for pinning it, not for trusting it.
`job-manifest.test.ts` now pins it directly: a `runId` of `run_a.1` yields label
`run_a.1` and path component `runa1`.

**The issue's own analysis was wrong about `isolationKey`, and it is corrected
here.** `isolationKey` is *not* in that class: `resolveJobIsolation` sanitizes
the raw key once with `sanitizeForK8sPath` (falling back to `shortHash`), and
both the label and the path consume that single already-sanitized value — so for
it alone, label and path component are equal by construction. A test asserting
otherwise was written, failed, and was replaced rather than forced to pass.

That narrows the divergence class; it does not remove it, and the decision is
unchanged. A reconstruction that diverges computes a path that does not exist,
and a non-existent file is **indistinguishable from a successful reap**, because
`ENOENT` is the silent-and-correct case for the owning run. The failure mode
would be a silent no-op — precisely the shape BLO-32734 existed to remove,
re-introduced from the other end.

So `buildJobManifest` stamps the already-computed `podLogPath` onto the Job as
`paperclip.io/pod-log-path`, and the reaper reads it back verbatim. There is no
divergence class left to reason about. `job-manifest.test.ts` asserts the
annotation equals the builder's own returned `podLogPath`, in both the plain and
isolated branches, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

## It supersedes BLO-37704, which took the reconstruction route

While this PR sat, `6e822b8` ("reap the stale run's pod log when the guard
deletes its Job", BLO-37704) landed on master and fixed the *same* defect by the
*other* route — a `podLogPathForForeignJob()` that rebuilds the path from the
Job's labels. That is the route BLO-39114's own analysis rejected, for the
sanitizer-divergence reason tabulated above, and its commit message addresses
only the `isolationMode`/`isolationKey` divergence, not the
`sanitizeForK8sPath` vs `sanitizeLabelValue` one.

The two cannot coexist at one call site, so the rebase removes the
reconstruction: `podLogPathForForeignJob()`, its `sanitizeForK8sPath` import in
`execute.ts`, and its three `describe("stale-Job pod-log reaping")` tests. Its
coverage is not lost — the surviving test exercises the same branch end to end
against a real file in `os.tmpdir()` rather than a spy, and the isolation
segment it probed is now structurally guaranteed, because the annotation is
stamped from `buildPodLogPath`'s own output instead of being recomputed.

`sanitizeForK8sPath` stays exported in `job-manifest.ts`. Unexporting it is
unrelated churn in a file this PR already touches for a different reason.

## Reporting a miss

`reapPodLogFile` grew a `reportMissing` flag, off by default, set only on the
foreign-run reap. For the owning run `ENOENT` must stay silent or every clean
run emits noise. For a foreign reap the caller asked for a *specific* file by
reading an annotation, so a miss carries information — and the two kinds of
miss mean different things, so they go to different streams:

- **no annotation** → `stderr` warning. The Job predates this change; we know a
  file was left on the PVC. That is the leak, and it must not be silent.
- **annotation present, file absent** → `stdout` note. Nothing leaked; the pod
  most likely died before writing a log. Reported, but not a warning.

The issue's AC asked for a miss to be reported on the grounds that it "means
the reconstruction is broken". That rationale is specific to the reconstruction
route, which this change does not take — under the stamped-annotation route a
miss is usually benign. The report is kept anyway (silence is what hid the
original leak), but graded so it does not cry wolf on every orphan.

## The consumer-side guard checks shape, not root

`fs.unlink` now acts on a path read off a **mutable** Kubernetes object, so the
read site screens it with `isReapablePodLogPath` before handing it to
`cleanupJob`: absolute, ends `.pod.ndjson`, no `..` segment. A rejected
annotation is warned about and dropped — but the Job is still deleted, or a
file leak would become a Job leak.

It checks *shape* rather than containment under `/paperclip/instances/default/data/run-logs`,
and that is a deliberate trade, not an oversight. Every pod-log test in the
suite writes into `os.tmpdir()`, so a literal-root check could only be asserted
by writing into the real PVC or by adding a test-only env seam — an untested
guard on a destructive primitive is worse than a tested narrower one. The named
hazard class (a kubeconfig, a Secret file, a source file) is blocked by the
suffix clause. `POD_LOG_ROOT` is therefore **not** exported: the root literal
has no consumer, and a comment at the producer claiming otherwise would point
the next reader at a defence that is not there.

All three clauses are mutation-covered by `describe("isReapablePodLogPath")` in
`execute.test.ts` — one assertion per clause, so deleting any one of them
reddens exactly one assertion *in that block*. Fleet-wide the suffix clause
reddens one more: the integration test's `not-a-pod-log.yaml` fixture is
already absolute and `..`-free, so it pins the suffix and nothing else, and
dropping that clause unlinks the bystander there too.

## Scope limit, stated plainly

A Job created **before** this change carries no annotation, so its log is not
reaped — the warning above is the only thing that will say so. Those Jobs age
out via `ttlSecondsAfterFinished`. This closes the producer; it does not
retroactively collect what already leaked.

`warnQuietly` became `logQuietly(onLog, stream, message)` — same
never-throw behaviour, now able to write either stream. Both existing call
sites are unchanged in behaviour.
